title: Philosophy for kids: what is real?
examples: If I dream I can fly, does that mean flying is real?
How can we be sure that our senses are always telling us the truth?
What is the difference between what seems real and what is actually real?

explain.say: Today we explore what it means to be real. We will think about what we experience in our minds.

draw.text: Philosophy for kids: what is real?

items: Reality is what is truly real.
It is what exists outside our minds.

explain.say: First we look at dreams. In dreams, things can happen that are not possible when awake. For example, you might dream you can talk to animals.
Next we look at appearances. Appearances are how things seem to us right now. For example, a stick in water looks bent, but it is not really bent.
Then we consider how we know things. Knowing something means we have good evidence for it. For example, seeing the sun rise gives us strong evidence of the day.
In everyday life, think about a photograph. The picture looks like a real person, but it is just ink on paper. This shows appearances can fool us.
A common mistake is assuming that because we see it, it must be real. You might think a loud noise means a real monster is there. We must check our knowledge.

items: Does it mean it is real?

faq.q: If I dream something, was it real when I was dreaming?
faq.a: It was real to you while you were experiencing it in the dream. However, it did not exist in the waking world.

faq.q: Can my senses ever trick me into thinking something is real?
faq.a: Yes, our senses can be tricked by illusions, like seeing a mirage in the heat. This shows appearances are not always the truth.
asks: Can I be fooled by what I see?

faq.q: What is the difference between an appearance and reality?
faq.a: Appearance is how something seems to us, which can be misleading. Reality is what something is actually like, regardless of how it seems.
asks: What is the difference between seeming and being?
Is appearance the same as reality?

faq.q: How do philosophers decide what is truly real?
faq.a: Philosophers use logic and questioning to test our assumptions. They ask for evidence that cannot be explained by illusion or misunderstanding.
asks: What is the test for reality?
How do we prove something exists?

faq.q: Does the fact that I can tell you about it make it real?
faq.a: No, just talking about something does not make it real. We need evidence that exists independently of our thoughts.
asks: Is thought enough to make something real?

facts: Dreams are mental experiences that occur during sleep.
An illusion is something that deceives the senses.
Knowledge requires evidence that supports a belief.
Philosophy questions the nature of existence itself.

quiz.say: If you see a rainbow, is the rainbow itself a physical object?
quiz.why: A rainbow is an optical phenomenon, an appearance caused by light, not a solid, independently existing object.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it seems visible, but visibility does not guarantee physical reality.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it seems too vague, but we must categorize it based on our understanding of perception.
wrong.2: This is tempting because the rainbow is so colorful, but color is a property of light, not a substance.

quiz.say: Which is the best way to test if something is real?

options.show: If someone tells you it is real
options.say: If someone tells you it is real

quiz.why: Good knowledge requires evidence that holds up under logical testing, not just initial impact.

wrong.0: Belief from others is not enough; you must verify the claim yourself.
wrong.2: Appearance can be easily fooled, as seen with optical illusions.
wrong.3: Emotions are powerful, but they are subjective and do not prove objective reality.
